messages.subject: Drawing Modified World map using 'geom_map'
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to draw a world map, however slightly with different
inputs. I am basically performing various what-if type of analysis
combining various adjacent countries and then checking how a specific
parameter is changing. An example is below :

library(rworldmap)
library(ggplot2)
map.world = map_data(map="world")
map.world$name_len = nchar(map.world$region) + sample(nrow(map.world))

Now let say, I combine USA & Canada and name this combination as
'Super Country' :

map.world1 = map.world
map.world1[map.world1[, 'region'] == 'USA', 'region'] = 'Super Country'
map.world1[map.world1[, 'region'] == 'Canada', 'region'] = 'Super Country'

gg = ggplot()
gg = gg + theme(legend.position="none")
gg = gg + geom_map(data=map.world1, map=map.world1, aes(map_id=region,
x=long, y=lat, fill=name_len))
gg

So far, it is good. However I still see in the ggplot that the
Boundary between US & Canada is very prominent, so my 'Super Country'
is not really looking as a 'single country'.

I have tried with putting 'colour = NA' attribute, however it is not
changing anything :

> gg = ggplot()

> gg = gg + theme(legend.position="none")

> gg = gg + geom_map(data=map.world1, map=map.world1, aes(map_id=region, x=long, y=lat, fill=name_len), colour = NA)

Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: x, y

> gg


Can you please suggest how can I hide the boundary between US &
Canada. And broadly how to remove the country boundaries for all
countries in the Map.

Appreciate for any pointer.

Thanks for your time.
